You are an independent classifier in a blinded experiment about a book of
biblical symbolism. The consensus responses below were produced without access
to the book. Compare them with the book's entry.

TERM
New moon

BLIND CONSENSUS RESPONSES
RESPONSE A
{
  "primary_meaning": "In mainstream Christian teaching the 'new moon' is understood primarily as part of Israel's ceremonial calendar of appointed times, and its symbolic significance is defined by Colossians 2:16-17: it is a 'shadow of things to come,' a type pointing forward to Christ, in whom the ceremonial observance finds its fulfillment. Because it marks the beginning of a month, it is commonly given the associated sense of renewal and new beginnings, with the fulfillment located in the newness of life in Christ rather than in continued calendrical observance.",

    "Colossians 2:16-17 (new moons as a shadow of things to come, the substance belonging to Christ)",
    "Numbers 28:11-15 (prescribed new moon offerings)",
    "Numbers 10:10 and Psalm 81:3 (trumpet blowing at the new moon)",
    "1 Samuel 20:5, 18, 24-27 (new moon feast in Israel's life)",
    "2 Kings 4:23 and Amos 8:5 (new moon as a recognized day of worship and cessation of commerce)",
    "Isaiah 66:23 (from new moon to new moon all flesh will worship the LORD)",
    "Ezekiel 46:1-6 (new moon worship in the temple vision)"
  ],

      "meaning": "Eschatological perpetual worship: Isaiah 66:23 (and Ezekiel 46) are read as a picture of continual, rhythmic worship of God in the new creation or millennial age, with the new moon symbolizing the ongoing cycle of devotion; some premillennial and dispensational interpreters take this as literal future observance.",

      "meaning": "Symbol of renewal, restoration, and monthly rededication (Rosh Chodesh): drawing on Jewish tradition, some Messianic, Hebrew-roots, and devotional writers treat the new moon as a symbol of Israel's (or the believer's) renewal, sometimes linking the waxing moon to Israel's restoration or the church reflecting the light of Christ as the moon reflects the sun.",
      "basis": [

        "Isaiah 66:23",

        "Colossians 2:16 (reread as defending observance from critics)",
        "Isaiah 66:23",
        "Numbers 28:11-15"
      ],
      "prominence": "minority"
    },
    {

        "Genesis 1:14 (lights as signs for appointed times)",
        "Psalm 104:19",
        "Numbers 28-29 calendar texts"
      ],
      "prominence": "rare"
    }
  ],
  "has_settled_consensus": true,
  "confidence": "medium",
  "notes": "There is a recognizable mainstream consensus, but it is a modest one: the new moon is rarely given rich standalone symbolism in Christian interpretation. It is almost always treated as one member of the triad 'festival, new moon, sabbath' (Colossians 2:16; Isaiah 1:13-14; Hosea 2:11), and its meaning is derived from that ceremonial-shadow framework rather than from an independent symbolic tradition. The renewal/new-beginnings reading is popular in devotional and Messianic literature but is less established in classical commentary. Interpreters divide mainly over whether Isaiah 66:23 is literal future observance, symbolic perpetual worship, or hyperbolic prophetic idiom; that dispute does not disturb the dominant 'shadow fulfilled in Christ' reading."
}

Colossians 2:16–17 supplies the clearest distinctively Christian typological interpretation."

BOOK ENTRY
The renewed moon — chodesh, from chadash, to renew: the phase of the moon that serves as the sign of the start of the month, and so the name of the month itself. A sign must be watched for: the east gate opens on it for worship, commerce resents it, and Paul files it among the shadows of things to come; which phase renews the month, the Pearl chapter weighs from the letters.

AVAILABLE KJV EXCERPTS
Psalms 81:3 — Blow up the trumpet in the new moon, in the time appointed, on our solemn feast day.
1 Samuel 20:5 — And David said unto Jonathan, Behold, to morrow is the new moon, and I should not fail to sit with the king at meat: but let me go, that I may hide myself in the field unto the third day at even.
1 Samuel 20:18 — Then Jonathan said to David, To morrow is the new moon: and thou shalt be missed, because thy seat will be empty.
Isaiah 66:23 — And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the LORD.
Ezekiel 46:1 — Thus saith the Lord GOD; The gate of the inner court that looketh toward the east shall be shut the six working days; but on the sabbath it shall be opened, and in the day of the new moon it shall be opened.
Ezekiel 46:2 — And the prince shall enter by the way of the porch of that gate without, and shall stand by the post of the gate, and the priests shall prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he shall worship at the threshold of the gate: then he shall go forth; but the gate shall not be shut until the evening.
Ezekiel 46:3 — Likewise the people of the land shall worship at the door of this gate before the LORD in the sabbaths and in the new moons.
Amos 8:5 — Saying, When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?
Colossians 2:16 — Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days:
Colossians 2:17 — Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.

CLASSIFY THE RELATIONSHIP

First reduce both readings to their minimum core identifications. Do not let
extra detail create an artificial disagreement.

- MATCH: the core identifications are equivalent. Differences are merely
  wording or immaterial detail.
- REFINED: the book preserves the consensus's general referent or category but
  materially changes its extension, boundary, conditions, or precision. A
  narrowing may reject some cases the broader consensus admits; a broadening
  may admit cases it excludes. This is real disagreement at the boundary, but
  not replacement of the central referent.
- DIVERGENT: the cores materially contradict. Both claims cannot be true of the
  same referent in the same context and sense; accepting the book requires
  rejecting or replacing the consensus identification. A source and its
  product remain different referents when the book explicitly denies their
  identity, even if they are causally related.
- NOVEL: no recognizable consensus or listed alternative covers the book's
  core identification. Novelty is absence from consensus, not contradiction.

Use `core_relation` to expose the relationship at the center and
`extension_relation` to expose disagreement over the cases covered. A REFINED
verdict must state what cases the book adds, excludes, or reclassifies. A
DIVERGENT verdict must identify a replaced referent or material contradiction,
not merely a narrower boundary.

Treat the two axes independently. A core-divergent reading may still retain
some cases covered by the consensus while rejecting its central identification;
therefore DIVERGENT does not require disjoint extensions. Conversely, a
narrowed extension is REFINED only when the consensus's central referent or
category remains intact.

Also judge whether the citations printed with the glossary entry alone provide
strong, partial, or insufficient support. Do not yet decide whether a divergent
full chapter is persuasive; that is a separate stage.
